UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile information, personal details, nutrition goals, and application preferences within the Nutrify application. This data drives personalization and tracking.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. (Primary Key)

name.description: User's full name as provided during signup.

email.description: User's email address, used for authentication and communication.

onboardingCompleted.description: Flag indicating if the user has completed the initial onboarding wizard.

unitPreference.description: Preferred unit system for measurements (e.g., 'metric' for cm/kg, 'imperial' for ft/lbs).

goalType.description: User's primary nutrition goal (e.g., 'Lose Weight', 'Maintain Weight', 'Gain Weight', 'Eat Healthier').

dietaryPreferences.description: An array of dietary restrictions or preferences selected by the user (e.g., 'Vegan', 'Halal', 'Diabetic-Friendly').

dailyCalorieGoal.description: The user's target daily calorie intake.

proteinPercentageGoal.description: Target percentage of daily calories from protein (0-100).

carbsPercentageGoal.description: Target percentage of daily calories from carbohydrates (0-100).

fatPercentageGoal.description: Target percentage of daily calories from fats (0-100).

ironTargetMg.description: User's target daily iron intake in milligrams.

vitaminATargetMcg.description: User's target daily Vitamin A intake in micrograms.

profileImageUrl.description: URL to the user's profile picture.

languagePreference.description: User's preferred language for the application (e.g., 'English', 'Twi', 'Ewe').

reminderEnabled.description: Flag indicating if daily nutrition reminders are enabled for the user.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last update to the user profile.

FoodItem.title: FoodItem
FoodItem.description: Represents a single food item with its nutritional values and categorization.

id.description: Unique identifier for the FoodItem entity. (Primary Key)

name.description: The common name of the food item.

description.description: A brief description or general category of the food item.

imageUrl.description: URL to an image representing the food item.

caloriesPer100g.description: Nutritional value: Calories per 100 grams of the food.

proteinPer100g.description: Nutritional value: Protein in grams per 100 grams of the food.

carbsPer100g.description: Nutritional value: Carbohydrates in grams per 100 grams of the food.

fatPer100g.description: Nutritional value: Fats in grams per 100 grams of the food.

fiberPer100g.description: Nutritional value: Fiber in grams per 100 grams of the food.

ironPer100g.description: Nutritional value: Iron in milligrams per 100 grams of the food.

vitaminAPer100g.description: Nutritional value: Vitamin A in micrograms per 100 grams of the food.

sodiumPer100g.description: Nutritional value: Sodium in milligrams per 100 grams of the food.

category.description: Primary category of the food item (e.g., 'Fruits', 'Proteins', 'Local Dishes', 'Vegetables', 'International').

isGhanaianLocal.description: Flag indicating if the food item is considered a local Ghanaian dish or ingredient.

smallServingGrams.description: Weight in grams for a 'Small' portion size of this food. (Optional)

mediumServingGrams.description: Weight in grams for a 'Medium' portion size of this food. (Optional)

largeServingGrams.description: Weight in grams for a 'Large' portion size of this food. (Optional)

DailyFoodLog.title: DailyFoodLog
DailyFoodLog.description: Records a specific food item consumed by a user at a given meal time on a particular date.

id.description: Unique identifier for a daily food log entry. (Primary Key)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who logged this food. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N DailyFoodLog)

foodId.description: Reference to the FoodItem that was logged. (Relationship: FoodItem 1:N DailyFoodLog)

mealType.description: The meal category for which the food was logged (e.g., 'Breakfast', 'Lunch', 'Dinner', 'Snacks').

logDate.description: The specific date (YYYY-MM-DD) on which the food was consumed.

portionGrams.description: The amount of the food item consumed in grams.

loggedCalories.description: The total calculated calories for this specific food portion at the time of logging.

loggedProtein.description: The total calculated protein in grams for this specific food portion at the time of logging.

loggedCarbs.description: The total calculated carbohydrates in grams for this specific food portion at the time of logging.

loggedFat.description: The total calculated fats in grams for this specific food portion at the time of logging.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when this food entry was logged.

MealPlan.title: MealPlan
MealPlan.description: Represents a planned food item for a user on a specific day of the week and meal type.

id.description: Unique identifier for a meal plan entry. (Primary Key)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile for whom this meal is planned. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N MealPlan)

foodId.description: Reference to the FoodItem that is planned. (Relationship: FoodItem 1:N MealPlan)

mealType.description: The meal category for which the food is planned (e.g., 'Breakfast', 'Lunch', 'Dinner', 'Snacks').

planDayOfWeek.description: The day of the week for which this meal is planned (e.g., 'Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Sunday').

portionGrams.description: The amount of the food item planned in grams.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when this meal plan entry was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last update to this meal plan entry.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by strictly adhering to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence and Queryable by Authorization Predicate (QAP).

1.  **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}`):** User profiles are stored in a top-level collection, with the document ID (`{userId}`) directly matching the Firebase Authentication UID. This establishes a clear, path-based ownership model where a user's profile document (`resource.id`) is unequivocally tied to their authenticated identity (`request.auth.uid`). This direct mapping ensures Authorization Independence as rules for user profiles (`allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == resource.id;`) do not require any `get()` operations, making them atomic and highly performant.

2.  **User-Specific Subcollections (`/users/{userId}/dailyFoodLogs` and `/users/{userId}/mealPlans`):** For user-owned data like daily food logs and meal plans, a hierarchical path structure is used. These are placed as subcollections under the respective user's profile, e.g., `/users/{userId}/dailyFoodLogs/{dailyFoodLogId}`. This design is critical for Authorization Independence and QAPs:
    *   **Authorization Independence:** The `{userId}` wildcard in the path template directly exposes the owner's UID to the security rules. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls to a parent document to determine ownership. Rules can simply state `allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == userId;`. Furthermore, each document in these subcollections includes an explicit `userId` field, which acts as a denormalized `ownerId`. This field can be used in rules for an additional layer of validation (`request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId`), ensuring data integrity and preventing unauthorized data injection, without breaking atomicity.
    *   **QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** This structure inherently supports secure `list` operations. When a user queries `/users/{request.auth.uid}/dailyFoodLogs`, the security rules enforce that the `{userId}` in the path must match `request.auth.uid`. Therefore, the query can only ever return data belonging to the authenticated user, satisfying the QAP principle by ensuring that `list` operations are naturally secure and do not expose unauthorized data.

3.  **Global Food Database (`/foodItems`):** The `foodItems` collection is a top-level collection designed for global access. It contains static, publicly readable data about various food items. Since this data is intended to be available to all authenticated users for search and reference, its security posture is homogeneously 'publicly readable by authenticated users'. This segregates it from private user data and simplifies its security rules, ensuring that `list` operations on this collection are inherently secure as they are intended to return globally available data.

Overall, this structure employs path-based ownership and strategic denormalization (explicit `userId` fields in subcollections) to achieve Authorization Independence. It uses structural segregation to define homogeneous security postures for collections and subcollections, which directly enables robust QAPs. This leads to simple, efficient, and easily debuggable Firestore security rules.
